label: PF Backlog 673
title: Structured outbox metrics and alerting for event authority
body: BI-PF-1268 left outbox-bound backpressure with log-only observability. Add structured metrics for pending/claimed outbox rows, bound rejections, prune counts and projection failures so operators can alert across instances without parsing stderr.

objective: Structured outbox metrics and alerting for event authority
acceptance_criteria: Expose an outbox_rows_current gauge by tenant/status and an EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED counter, with owner and alert threshold documented and tested.
Emit structured outbox prune and projection-failure signals through the existing observability owner, not ad-hoc stderr logging, and verify them in tests.

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=3bd78fc68352
BLOCKER:
  - CL-010 violated: proof_plan red_evidence = 'absent'; no current-run red/failing proof for the real metrics exporter entrypoint — declared tests/prose are not proof.
  - AC-1 requires owner + alert threshold documented and tested; design names no threshold value and no accountable owner (only "existing metrics owner") — AC unverifiable as written.
MAJOR:
  - Evidence conflict: functional_spec traceability points AC-1/AC-2 to go/edpdata/event_metrics_test.go, design_pack coverage points to tests/test_review_material_change.py — neither is shown to assert the gauge, counter, or structured prune/projection-failure signals.
  - CL-001 unresolved: "existing metrics owner"/observability owner is never named or registered as single writer; no route-by-kind decision proving no duplicate exporter/registry is introduced.
  - Label cardinality contradiction: invariant "metrics are tenant-scoped" vs guardrail "no high-cardinality tenant-id labels" — tenant label set must be bounded (allow-list/registry) before Gate 1.5.
  - CL-012 not addressed: outbox_rows_current implies repeated row counts; runtime_contract pins no count bounding, refresh/cache interval, or statement_timeout for the scrape path.
MINOR:
  - Gate-1 context has affected_components/affected_files "Not specified" while design_pack declares 5 files — sync needed per CL-006.
  - Checklist items 1-6, 8-9 unanswered: no alert lead-time / exporter-down detection story; rollback is "remove metrics" with no cleanup of dashboards/alert rules.
  - out_of_scope and risks are "Not specified"; config_contract artifact is only config/review-budget.json with no metric-specific config key.
NIT:
  - FR-2 title truncated mid-sentence in functional_spec; failure_matrix covers only 'missing metric', not absence of prune/projection-failure signals.
  - spec_pack release_verification cites one generic test file as evidence for every APPLICABLE spec.
SUMMARY:
  - Not ready for Gate 1.5: missing red proof (CL-010) and undocumented owner/threshold make AC-1/AC-2 unverifiable as designed.
  - Top risks: contradictory test evidence, unresolved tenant-label cardinality, unnamed single-writer ownership, and unbounded scrape-time counting.
  - Direction is right (reuse existing metrics owner, Go-only files, low-cardinality guardrail); close the four MAJORs and answer the checklist before approval.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=e1b56e43559b
BLOCKER:
  - AC-1 not met: no real metrics implementation or registration anywhere in the diff — `EventMetrics` only has a `nopEventMetrics` default and no shipped caller of `WithMetrics`, so `outbox_rows_current` / `EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED` are never exposed to any scraper (spec's failure matrix: "missing signal blocks release").
  - AC-1 "owner and alert threshold documented" unmet: the diff contains no documentation change (no runbook/design doc) stating the metric owner or the alert threshold; `docs/EVENTING-ALERTING-SSOT-DESIGN.md` is cited as evidence but is not in the diff.
MAJOR:
  - New `EventMetrics` interface invented inside `edpdata` instead of reusing the existing Prometheus-compatible observability owner the design assumes ("Use existing metrics owner", CL-001 single-writer/ownership) — parallel metric owners and duplicated registration risk.
  - Gauge is emitted only as a side effect inside `EnforceOutboxBound`, not via a scrape-time collector: tenants/paths that don't run bound enforcement report no or stale gauge, so "when metrics are scraped, then outbox rows are visible" fails.
  - Only the hardcoded status `"pending"` label is ever produced; AC-1 requires the gauge by tenant/status, other statuses are never reported.
  - Tests only assert calls into a local `recordingMetrics` stub; nothing verifies the real owner exposes an `outbox_rows_current` gauge or a counter named/evented `EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED`, so AC "tested" is against a fake contract.
  - AC-2 "not ad-hoc stderr logging": `log.Printf("EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED ...")` is retained in `EnforceOutboxBound` alongside the new metric, leaving two divergent emission paths for the same signal.
MINOR:
  - `OutboxBoundExceeded(tenant)` discards pending/max values carried by the log line, so the structured signal is strictly less diagnosable than the log it is meant to replace.
  - `ProjectionFailed(tenant)` drops the error/reason; the detail remains only in the response body (`projection_error`), reducing post-hoc diagnosis.
  - `WithMetrics` mutates a live `EventStore` field without synchronization; racy if attached after the store is serving (interface itself demands concurrency safety).
  - `OutboxPruned` is skipped whenever `err != nil`, so partially-applied prunes (n > 0 with error) produce no signal.
NIT:
  - `recordingMetrics` counters are not concurrency-safe despite the interface contract; harmless today but will mask races if tests go parallel.
  - `nopEventMetrics` methods could be grouped, and `RecordProjectionFailure` is a one-line wrapper only used at a single call site.
SUMMARY:
  - Direction (interface-based observability owner in Go, tenant-scoped signals, unit tests) is right, but the AC is not delivered: no real metric implementation/wiring, no owner/threshold documentation, and gauge semantics are push-on-demand rather than scrape-time.
  - Top risks: release-blocking "missing signal", a second metrics owner alongside the assumed Prometheus one, and tests that only prove the stub contract.
  - Recommend blocking until a real owner is wired, documentation lands, and tests assert the exported metric names/labels.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
